chapter: Chano Pozo, Town Hall and Charlie Parker
title: No rivalry with Noro Morales and Marcelino Guerra
summary: Machito says mature bandleaders with settled styles did not feel rivalry, unlike Puente and Rodriguez, and that there were fewer bands then.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Did you ever have any rivalry with Marcelino Guerra?

No, no. I - let me tell you - I am so sure that what I am doing is close to the right thing that I know practically - because this music, I've been involved in my music for so long, that I know when somebody had a good band. I have a different way of explain or to present what I feel in my music, because everybody has his own feeling. Like Duke Ellington, one of the finest musician, that had very creative mind; but Duke Ellington doesn't sound like Count Basie......
.... and both was two good bands. Fletcher Henderson ..... .

No, I understand all that, but was there any rivalry with any band? Did they force you into it? Not that you wanted to, but were you forced into rivalry with Noro Morales, with Marcelino Guerra, or any of the top bands at the time? You know, the rivalry that Puente and Rodriguez had. Were you ever......
No, you didn't have no rivalry?

No, no, no, no. Well, they was mature people. Noro Morales was in his early forties, maybe late thirties, I was in the late thirties or maybe early forties and we had a different conception. We was so involved and enjoyed ourselves and to listen to a good music that when Noro Morales was there I didn't dance, I was listening to Noro Morales to enjoy what he had to offer. This is a different - ehhh, when you get into a certain age or you are sure that you have a definite style, you don't change your style or you don't get excited because another band play in his style very good. The only thing you have to do when you have you play, play what you know; not playing harder to do better, because right there you start to lose your touch.
Uh - Huh. Macho, that was the late forties. Now, correct me if I am wrong. The most, the top number of bands was probably about thirty. Am I right?
No, I don't think that we had thirty bands.
You didn't have that much, right?
Okay, so there was work for a lot of people in different places. It isn't the competitive thing that it is today, in 1980, when you got about 400 bands now.
Well, but is different. In those days there was mature people competing to have a good reputation, good service, good organization, good band; clean with beautiful uniform, be on time ......
